transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO), Maya Patel (Lead ML Eng), Ravi Kapoor (Head Infra)

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intros and then dig into cost stuff. i'm liam, i'm the AE working with aurora, and sofia is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Daniel: thanks liam, yeah hi i'm daniel, cto at aurora, maya and ravi are with me. main reason for call is we need to understand unit economics — we have a budget target for q2 and want to see if hosted makes sense or we should go dedicated or private.
[00:27] Sofia: great, can you share a bit about your workload? latency needs, token volumes, and sensitive data concerns?
[00:34] Maya: sure. primary workload is a customer-facing summarization + retrieval augmented generation flow. average request ~1.2k tokens in, we expect ~700 tokens generated on average. Peak concurrent requests ~120, average rps ~6. we estimate ~200M tokens/month generation. some PII in prompts so we care about data residency but can work with hosted if retention & encryption controls are ok.
[00:56] Liam: awesome, that helps. so high-level — hosted is easiest and has per-token pricing, dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, private is for strict residency or air-gapped needs. what are your budget constraints?
[01:10] Daniel: we have an internal goal of under $0.0025 per generated token equivalent for the feature at 200M tokens/month, if possible. open to tradeoffs on latency up to 100-200ms tail increase.
[01:23] Sofia: okay so we should walk through how per-token unit cost is composed — model price, effective tokens per call, and system-level savings like batching and KV cache. also quantization/half-precision model variants reduce cost per token.
[01:36] Ravi: quick question — how predictable are costs with hosted? we want to avoid big bill shock.
[01:41] Liam: hosted is usage-based so it's variable, we provide monthly forecasts and rate limits, but if you need predictability Dedicated offers reserved capacity with commit discounts. many customers start hosted and then commit to Dedicated when volumes justify it.
[01:52] Sofia: for a rough calc: take model generation price x tokens generated, then subtract savings from batching (up to 20-40% on throughput tokens) and KV/prefix caching (can avoid repeated encode cost for long contexts). also concurrency and request size influence GPU efficiency — more continuous batching yields lower cost per token.
[02:12] Maya: curious about batching window — if we increase batching to 50ms or 100ms what's the latency impact and savings?
[02:18] Sofia: so there's a tradeoff: typical batching windows of 20-50ms are common in low-latency settings; 50-100ms can improve throughput a fair bit but adds tail latency. with our runtime tuning we often hit sweet spot around 30-40ms for chat/summaries. savings depend on model size and request shape; for your 700-gen token average, batching could reduce token compute by ~15-25% in practice.
[02:40] Daniel: and KV cache — for RAG flows how effective is prefix caching? our prompts reuse retrieval context a lot.
[02:47] Sofia: very effective for RAG. if the retrieval chunk is repeated across requests, KV cache keeps key/value states so subsequent generation avoids re-encoding that context. in real workloads we see 20-60% reduction in compute depending on reuse patterns. we'll want your retrieval traces to estimate.
[03:02] Ravi: what's the delta in per-token price between hosted and Dedicated?
[03:06] Liam: depends on commit size and model. rough ballpark: hosted might be $0.0035-$0.006 per generated token for large advanced models; Dedicated can get you to sub-$0.002 to $0.003 per token with committed capacity and optimized kernels, plus further reductions from quantization. we'll send a detailed sheet.
[03:22] Maya: you mentioned quantization — do you support 4-bit/8-bit or other quantized runtimes in Hosted? Any quality tradeoffs we should expect?
[03:30] Sofia: yes, our runtime supports INT8/4-bit style quantized variants for many open models. quality impact is model-dependent; for many summarization tasks you can use 8-bit with minimal regression. we can run quick evals on your prompts to compare. quantization typically reduces GPU memory and can improve throughput so cost drops.
[03:47] Daniel: on security — SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs — how does Hosted handle encryption keys and retention?
[03:55] Liam: hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for encryption at-rest, SOC2 compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. Private gives the most control (customer VPC, full data plane control). we'll attach our security pack.
[04:09] Ravi: if we move to Dedicated, can we burst to hosted during spikes?
[04:13] Sofia: yes, we offer hybrid routing policies — burst to hosted or fallback to smaller models to maintain latency. that's a common pattern.
[04:20] Maya: let's talk numbers — if we assume 200M gen tokens/month and 0.003 per token baseline, that's $600k/mo — too high for us. to hit daniel's goal of 0.0025/token we'd need either discounts, batching/cache savings, or dedicated commit. can you sketch scenarios?
[04:36] Liam: quick math: 200M * 0.003 = $600k. If Dedicated brings to 0.002 with commit discount that's $400k. Add KV/batching savings 20% effective means effective cost could be $0.0016/token giving $320k/mo. Quantization might push further. We'll produce an itemized model.
[04:54] Daniel: ok that makes sense. we need that spreadsheet. also want to pilot with 2 weeks of traffic to measure real-world savings.
[05:02] Sofia: recommended POC: run three variants — hosted as-is on curated model, hosted with kv caching enabled + batching config, and Dedicated small commit with quantized model. we'll run same prompt set, capture latency, throughput, and cost per effective token.
[05:18] Maya: what's the engineering effort on our side for POC?
[05:22] Liam: minimal — we provide a quickstart, SDKs, and a small config file to enable KV caching/batching. SE will help with setup and a short runbook.
[05:29] Ravi: any compliance blockers for us to share data traces? we need to anonymize PII.
[05:33] Sofia: yeah, please scrub PII or we can run the tests in your VPC/Private so data never leaves your environment. for initial benchmarks scrubbed traces are fine.
[05:40] Daniel: what about retention and logging costs — do logs count towards tokens or is that separate?
[05:45] Liam: logs and telemetry are billed separately as part of observability addon; they don't count as model tokens. token billing is only for model input/output.
[05:52] Maya: any limits on max sequence length or KV cache size per session?
[05:56] Sofia: we support long contexts but the effective behavior depends on model variant and memory/kv storage. we can tune config per POC.
[06:02] (discussion continues through architecture tradeoffs and examples)
[35:10] Sofia: quick demo snippet — here is a sample benchmark config we'll run: batch window 30ms, max batch 64, kv cache ttl 600s, quantize int8 for the medium-large model. we'll record tokens saved and effective throughput.
[35:28] Daniel: sounds good. for SLOs we target p95 latency <600ms for generate portion.
[35:34] Sofia: we can target that; if dedicated capacity required we'll size GPUs to meet that p95 with your concurrency.
[35:40] Liam: recap — deliverables: pricing sheet + cost model, POC config and benchmark plan, security pack. next call to review results and sizing.
[35:50] Daniel: thanks all — we'll share sample traces and confirm timeline.
[35:55] Liam: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and docs.

End transcript (approx 48m). Note: auto-transcription had minor mislabels and filler words; recommended to treat transcript as rough and rely on next steps and attachments for concrete numbers.
